image_alt: Two-panel forest plot separates Munich Chronotype Questionnaire corrected midsleep on free days from Morningness–Eveningness Questionnaire associations. Each panel shows primary near-eye and complementary chest estimates, distinguished by colour and shape, with 95% CIs for the five registered timing outcomes. Corrected-midsleep estimates for M10 midpoint, L10 midpoint, and first time above 250 lx melEDI tend positive, while morning-preference estimates for those outcomes tend negative.
caption: Figure 1: Study-site-adjusted chronotype associations with midpoint of the brightest 10 hours (M10 midpoint), midpoint of the darkest 10 hours (L10 midpoint), first and last time above 250 lx melEDI, and midpoint of the longest continuous period above 250 lx melEDI. Near-eye estimates are primary and chest estimates complementary; colour and shape identify placement, and horizontal bars are 95% CIs.

image_alt: Equal-axis scatter plot compares near-eye estimates horizontally with chest estimates vertically for five timing metrics in separate MCTQ MSFsc and MEQ panels. Each point has horizontal and vertical 95% CIs, with zero lines and a dashed identity line.
caption: Figure 2: Near-eye and chest chronotype associations fitted separately for the same participants and participant-days. Horizontal and vertical bars are component 95% CIs; the dashed diagonal is an identity reference and is not an equivalence boundary.

image_alt: Twenty-four near-eye model-check panels show residuals versus fitted timing in the upper half and normal-score Q-Q plots in the lower half. Some first-above-250 and L10 panels depart more at the tails than other outcomes, while the overall patterns were judged acceptable.
caption: Figure 3: Near-eye residual-versus-fitted and normal-score Q-Q model checks for the six analysed timing outcomes and both chronotype instruments. Visual review supported acceptable response/residual distribution and heteroscedasticity assessments.

caption: Figure 4: Chest residual-versus-fitted and normal-score Q-Q model checks for the six analysed timing outcomes and both chronotype instruments. Visual review supported acceptable response/residual distribution and heteroscedasticity assessments.
